caption: The drawing features a composition done in a sepia or reddish-brown monochrome ink on a plain, lightly yellowed background. At the top center of the image, there is a large, ornate oval object with decorative, draped elements and patterned details resembling embroidery or beadwork, possibly a ceremonial or cultural item. Below this, occupying the lower portion of the image, are figures and elements laid out in a horizontal arrangement. From left to right, there is a person holding a long stick or rifle directed upward, standing next to a bushy, rounded tree. Multiple birds, some in flight and others perched, are positioned above the tree and throughout the scene. Moving rightward, a smaller tree or bush appears, followed by a standing human figure. To the right of this person, a horse stands with its head lowered beside a bush. Further right, another bush is depicted, with two deer-like animals standing to the right of it, one closer and one further right. Grass and small plant motifs run along the entire lower border under the figures, providing a ground line. The entire composition is contained within a rectangular border, and "PLATE 2" is inscribed in the lower left corner, while a name and date—"Edward Lomax Del. 1834"—appear in the lower right corner.
title: Powder Horn
